mainTopic: Why בית שמאי rule differently in the two halves of the משנה about property that came to a שומרת יבם: אביי's explanation, רבא's challenge, and רבא's own answer based on מאמר.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the debate between אביי and רבא about property that came to a שומרת יבם. אביי holds that a husband's hold on his wife's property is only equal to hers. רבא instead says the two halves of the משנה differ by whether the יבם did a מאמר. The גמרא matches each view to an earlier authority and defends רבי אלעזר's position. רב פפא then says the wording of the משנה favors אביי, though the case of 'מתה' remains hard for him. Next, the גמרא explains that after יבום she is fully his wife: a גט ends the marriage and he may remarry her. Her כתובה, however, stays on the first husband's property unless he left nothing. A new משנה gives the eldest brother first duty for יבום and forbids stalling by waiting for another brother. The גמרא brings a מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי on whether a younger brother's יבום or the eldest's חליצה is better. It shows that the משנה cannot settle this, because we never delay a מצוה.

steps.title: What אביי assumes about the husband's hold on the property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the assumption behind אביי's answer: the husband's hold on his wife's property is equal to hers, not stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי holds that the husband's hand is like her hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining the reasoning behind אביי's answer, which came just before this. It tells us what אביי assumes about who has the stronger claim to the wife's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumes that, according to בית הלל, a husband's rights in his wife's property are only equal to hers. A יבם always has weaker rights than a real husband, so his claim is weaker than hers. That is why her own heirs keep the property. בית שמאי think the husband's hold is stronger, so the יבם ends up equal to her, and the two sides divide the property.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / he is of the opinion
His hand is like her hand: his hold on the property equals hers
אביי, the אמורא whose answer is being explained

phrases.english: And Abaye holds
his hand is like her hand.
phrases.notes: "Hand" here means a legal hold or claim on the property, not a physical hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the assumption behind אביי's resolution, which was given just before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אביי, in בית הלל's view a husband's hold on his wife's property equals hers and is not stronger.

steps.title: רבא objects that everyone agrees the husband's hold is stronger
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if the property came to her while her first husband was alive, both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree his hold is stronger than hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If the property came to her while she was under her husband, everyone agrees that his hand is stronger than her hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's explanation. He says that for property that came to her while she was married, nobody disputes that the husband's claim is stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer placed the second case at a time when she was still married to her first husband. He needed בית הלל to say that the husband's hold is only equal to hers. רבא says that in that situation even בית הלל would agree the husband's hold is stronger. If so, אביי's way of explaining the dispute falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Under the husband: while she was married to him
Everyone agrees; no one disputes
Is stronger / is preferable
Fell to her: property she inherited

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If the property fell to her
when she was under the husband,
everyone does not disagree,
phrases.notes: "Everyone" here means both בית שמאי and בית הלל.

phrases.english: that his hand is stronger than her hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אִי דְּנָפְלִי לָהּ כְּשֶׁהִיא תַּחְתָּיו דְּבַעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's assumption that, according to בית הלל, a husband's hold equals his wife's hold.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For property that came to her during the marriage, all agree that the husband's hold is stronger. So אביי's distinction cannot explain the dispute.

steps.title: רבא's own answer: both cases are during the wait for the יבם
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both halves of the משנה deal with property that came to her as a שומרת יבם. The first half is where the יבם did no מאמר, and the second half is where he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both cases are where the property came to her while she was waiting for the יבם. The first part is where he had not done a מאמר with her. The second part is where he had done a מאמר with her.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected אביי's approach, רבא offers a new way to explain the two halves of the משנה. Both cases happen at the same time, but one has a מאמר and one does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי split the two cases by when the property came to her. רבא instead splits them by what the יבם did. Without a מאמר, her own claim wins. After a מאמר, the יבם gains enough of a claim that the property is divided.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that: both cases
A widow waiting for her יבם to do יבום or חליצה
The first part / the last part of the משנה
A betrothal-like act a יבם does with the יבמה before יבום, from the Rabbis

phrases.english: Rather, both this and that
are where it fell to her when she was waiting for the yavam.
The first clause is where he did not perform a levirate betrothal with her,
the latter clause is where he did perform a levirate betrothal with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי דְּנָפְלוּ לָהּ כְּשֶׁהִיא שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי's approach, רבא offers his own resolution.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the cases (אוקימתא): the two halves differ by whether a מאמר was done, not by when the property came to her.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The halves differ by timing: one case during the marriage, the other while she was waiting for the יבם (אביי).
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are while she is waiting for the יבם. The first half is without a מאמר and the second half is with a מאמר (רבא).
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: both halves of the משנה are about property that came to a שומרת יבם. The only difference is whether the יבם did a מאמר.

steps.title: רבא's view of what a levirate betrothal accomplishes for בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that according to בית שמאי, a מאמר makes the יבמה definitely betrothed with respect to exempting her צרה, and possibly married with respect to dividing the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא holds that according to בית שמאי, a מאמר makes her definitely betrothed and possibly married. Definitely betrothed: to exempt her צרה. Possibly married: to divide the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבא's answer. It spells out what a מאמר does according to בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מאמר gives her a mixed status. She counts as truly betrothed, so the other widow (her צרה) is released from יבום and חליצה. She is also possibly married, which gives the יבם a partial claim. Because his claim is only partial, the property is divided between the two sides, which explains the second half of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Definitely betrothed
Possibly married
To push away the צרה: to exempt the other widow from יבום
To divide the property

phrases.english: And Rava holds
that according to Beit Shammai a levirate betrothal makes her
definitely betrothed and possibly married.
Definitely betrothed: to push away her rival wife,
phrases.notes: The צרה is the other widow of the dead brother. Once this one has a מאמר, the other no longer needs יבום or חליצה.

phrases.english: and possibly married: to divide the property.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָסָבַר רָבָא מַאֲמָר לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי עוֹשֶׂה וַדַּאי אֲרוּסָה וּסְפֵק נְשׂוּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבא's resolution in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, a מאמר makes the יבמה definitely betrothed with respect to exempting her צרה. It makes her possibly married with respect to dividing the property.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מאמר gives the יבם a partial claim, which is why בית שמאי divide the property in the second half of the משנה but not in the first.
steps.whatToRemember: For בית שמאי, a מאמר means ודאי ארוסה, which exempts the צרה, and ספק נשואה, which leads to dividing the property.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the מאמר makes her fully married. It only makes her possibly married. That is exactly why the property is split rather than given entirely to the יבם.

steps.title: Two Amoraim line up with רבא and אביי
steps.stepSummary: A teaching in the name of רבי אלעזר matches רבא, and a teaching in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא matches אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said in the name of רבי אלעזר like רבא, and it was said in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא like אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that each side of the אביי–רבא debate has an earlier authority behind it. This report sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the argument was between אביי and רבא. Now we learn that רבי אלעזר explained the משנה the way רבא did, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explained it the way אביי did.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (a report of an אמורא's teaching)
In the name of
In line with him, following his view

phrases.english: It was stated in the name of Rabbi Elazar
in line with Rava,
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר explained the משנה the way רבא did in the earlier steps.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתְּמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: and it was stated in the name of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina
in line with Abaye.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attaches earlier authorities to the two positions just laid out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר follows רבא's reading. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא follows אביי's reading.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's other statement seems to contradict רבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר said that according to בית שמאי a מאמר acquires only to push away the צרה. How can he agree with רבא?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי אלעזר really say this? But רבי אלעזר said: according to בית שמאי, a מאמר acquires her only to push away the צרה, and nothing more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the report that רבי אלעזר matches רבא, by bringing another statement of his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that for בית שמאי a מאמר makes her possibly married with respect to dividing the property. רבי אלעזר's word 'only' (בלבד) suggests that a מאמר does nothing for the property. So his statement seems to oppose רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: But did he really say this? (opens a challenge)
A יבם's betrothal of the יבמה by the Rabbis' rule, using money or a document
To push away, to exempt
The rival wife (another wife of the dead brother)

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Elazar say this?
But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
According to Beit Shammai, a ma'amar does not acquire
except to push away the rival wife alone!
phrases.notes: The word 'alone' is the problem. It sounds like a מאמר gives no rights to her property.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the attribution made in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אלעזר matches רבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר limits a מאמר to pushing away the צרה only. רבא gives it a property effect as well.

steps.title: Answer one: switch the names
steps.stepSummary: Reverse the names: רבי אלעזר matches אביי, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא matches רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's first answer is that the report got the names backwards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we swap the names, רבי אלעזר is on אביי's side. Then his statement that a מאמר does 'only' this fits perfectly, and the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it (swap the names of who said what)

phrases.english: Reverse it.
phrases.notes: Swap the two names from step 5: רבי אלעזר goes with אביי, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא goes with רבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 6 by changing the attribution.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר follows אביי, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא follows רבא.

steps.title: Answer two: keep the names and reread רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: Do not swap the names. By 'only to push away the צרה' רבי אלעזר meant that a גט alone is not enough and חליצה is still needed. He never said a מאמר has no effect on the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: really, don't reverse. רבי אלעזר would tell you: when I said that, I meant that a גט is not enough for her, and she also needs חליצה. But did I say that he doesn't acquire her with respect to dividing the property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. It keeps רבי אלעזר with רבא and explains what his limiting statement really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'only' is now read as being about how she is released. Because the מאמר is limited, a גט cannot free her, and she needs חליצה too. The word was never about property. So רבי אלעזר can still agree with רבא that a מאמר affects how the property is divided.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Really, in truth (keeping the original assumption)
The ceremony that releases a יבמה from the יבם
To divide the property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי אלעזר's 'only' as limiting what a מאמר can do in every area. In this answer, the limit is only about how she is released (a גט is not enough, so חליצה is needed). It says nothing against property rights.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
really, do not reverse;
Rabbi Elazar could say to you:
When I said it,
I meant that a get is not enough for her,
rather she also needs chalitzah.
That he does not acquire with respect to dividing the property,
did I say that?
phrases.notes: This question expects a 'no.' רבי אלעזר never denied the property effect, so he can agree with רבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 6 that keeps the original names.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the scope of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Only to push away the צרה' means a מאמר has no effect on the property.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Only' refers to how she is released (a גט is not enough, חליצה is needed). It does not deny the property effect, so רבי אלעזר still matches רבא.

steps.title: רב פפא: the משנה's wording supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the precise wording of the משנה fits אביי, even though the word 'מתה' (she died) is still hard for אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the precise reading of the משנה is like אביי, even though 'she died' is difficult for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a final judgment on the debate. The exact wording of the משנה leans toward אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא does two things at once. He says the careful reading of the משנה supports אביי. He also admits that the משנה's word 'מתה' still poses a difficulty for אביי's reading. So אביי is favored, but not without a problem left over.

keyTerms.meaning: A precise reading, an inference from exact wording
Our משנה
Even though
It is difficult (an unresolved problem)

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers protect רבי אלעזר's attribution: swap the names, or read his 'only' as being about חליצה and not about property. In the end, רב פפא says the wording of the משנה favors אביי, even though 'מתה' remains a difficulty for him.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The precise reading of the Mishnah is in line with Abaye,
even though 'she died' is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: דִּיּוּקָא דְּמַתְנִיתִין כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the attribution question and weighs the two readings against the משנה's wording.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The precise wording of the משנה supports אביי, though the word 'מתה' remains a difficulty for him.

steps.title: How the משנה's wording supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה calls the property 'entering and leaving with her.' 'Entering' means into the husband's domain, so the משנה is talking about property she had while still married. That fits אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'property that enters and leaves with her.' What does 'enters' mean, and what does 'leaves' mean? Doesn't it mean it enters the husband's domain, and leaves the husband's domain to go to the father's domain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining רב פפא's claim from Step 9 that the exact wording of the משנה fits אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'enters with her' only makes sense if the property came into the husband's control during the marriage. So the משנה is looking at the time when she was married to her first husband. That matches אביי's reading of the case, not רבא's.

keyTerms.meaning: As it teaches (introduces the wording of the משנה)
Property that enters and leaves with her
The husband's domain or control
The father's domain, meaning her father's family as heirs

phrases.english: As it teaches: property that enters and leaves with her,
What is 'enters' and what is 'leaves'?
Is it not that 'enters' means into the husband's domain,
and 'leaves' means out of the husband's domain into the father's domain?
phrases.notes: When she dies, the property leaves the husband's control and passes to her father's family.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the wording-based support for אביי that רב פפא mentioned in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's reading of the משנה: the case is about property she had during her first marriage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'נכסים הנכנסים ויוצאים עמה'.

steps.title: Why 'she died' is still hard for אביי
steps.stepSummary: The difficulty with 'מתה' is this: instead of arguing about the property itself after her death, בית שמאי and בית הלל could have argued about the produce while she is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though 'she died' is difficult: instead of arguing about the property itself and after death, let them argue about her lifetime and about the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of רב פפא's statement, which is the problem with the word 'מתה' for אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets its argument after her death and about the property itself. The גמרא asks why it did not choose an easier, more everyday case, such as who gets the produce (פירות) while she is still alive. The wording helps אביי, but the case the משנה chose still pulls against him.

keyTerms.meaning: She died (the case in the משנה)
The property itself (the main asset)
Produce or profits from the property
During her lifetime

phrases.english: And even though 'she died' is difficult,
instead of disputing over the property itself and after death,
let them dispute during her lifetime and over the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the remaining weakness that רב פפא admitted in Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case is about property from her married years, the משנה should have used the simpler case of produce during her lifetime, not the property itself after her death.

steps.title: Nothing more to add
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the discussion. The wording supports אביי, but 'מתה' remains a difficulty, and the matter is left there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is nothing more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the אביי and רבא discussion without fully settling it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both points stand side by side. The wording favors אביי, and the case of 'she died' is hard for him. The גמרא does not resolve this tension any further.

keyTerms.meaning: And there is nothing more (to say on this)

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's verdict: the wording 'enters and leaves with her' supports אביי, while 'מתה' remains a difficulty for him.

phrases.english: And there is nothing more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion begun in Steps 9 to 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's wording supports אביי, and the difficulty of 'מתה' stays unresolved.

steps.title: What does 'he married her, she is like his wife' teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that once the יבם married her she is his wife, and asks what practical law this teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he married her, she is etc.' For what law is this said?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and sets up a question about its practical meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems obvious that after יבום she is his wife. So the גמרא wants to know which specific law the משנה is trying to teach with these words.

keyTerms.meaning: He married her (did יבום)
For what law? What practical point is being taught?

phrases.english: If he married her, she is etc.
phrases.notes: The כו׳ means 'and so on.' The משנה continues: she is like his wife in every way.

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which practical law follows from the משנה's statement that after יבום she is like his wife.

steps.title: He divorces her with a גט and may take her back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers that the משנה teaches two things: after יבום he ends the marriage with a גט, and he may remarry her afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: It is to say that he divorces her with a גט and may take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13 with רבי יוסי בר חנינא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once יבום has taken place she is a full wife, so the marriage ends with a regular גט like any marriage. Also, after the divorce he may remarry her, just as a man may remarry his own divorced wife.

keyTerms.meaning: He divorces her
A bill of divorce
He takes her back (remarries her)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that after יבום she is treated like a regular wife, both for ending the marriage and for remarrying.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
To say that he divorces her with a bill of divorce
and takes her back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: לוֹמַר שֶׁמְּגָרְשָׁה בְּגֵט וּמַחְזִירָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After יבום he divorces her with a גט, and he may remarry her afterward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the יבם has married her, she is a full wife: the marriage ends with a גט, and he may later remarry her.

steps.title: Isn't divorcing her with a גט obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the first half of רבי יוסי בר חנינא's answer: why would we need to be told that the יבם ends the marriage with a גט?
steps.simpleTranslation: He divorces her with a גט. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the first thing רבי יוסי בר חנינא said the משנה teaches and asks why that needed to be said at all. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the יבם married her, she is his wife, and a wife is divorced with a גט. So the teaching seems to add nothing. The גמרא wants to find what wrong idea it is preventing.

keyTerms.meaning: he divorces her
a bill of divorce
it is obvious

phrases.english: He divorces her with a bill of divorce. Isn't that obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the first teaching listed in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why it is necessary to say that after יבום he divorces her with a גט.

steps.title: We might have thought only חליצה could end it
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק still uses the word 'ויבמה' after calling her his wife. So we might have thought the original יבום bond stays on her, and only חליצה, not a גט, could end it. The משנה teaches that a גט works.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought this: since it is written 'And take her to him as a wife, and do יבום with her,' the Torah is telling us that the original יבום bond is still on her. Then חליצה would work, but a גט would not. The משנה teaches us that a גט works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the mistake the teaching prevents. We might have thought a woman who went through יבום still needs חליצה to be released.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions 'ויבמה' after 'ולקחה לו לאשה.' That could suggest she is still in the יבום relationship even after marriage. By saying 'he divorces her with a גט,' the משנה shows the marriage is now a regular marriage that a גט ends.

keyTerms.meaning: it could enter your mind to say (you might have thought)
the original יבום bond
the ceremony that releases a יבמה from the יבם
it teaches us (this is what we learn)

steps.confusionAlert: The mistaken idea is not that she cannot be divorced at all. It is that only חליצה, not a גט, would end the bond.

phrases.english: It could enter your mind to say,
since it is written:
"And take her to him as a wife, and do יבום with her"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5. The point is that 'ויבמה' comes after he already took her as a wife.

phrases.english: the Merciful One is saying:
the original יבום bond is still upon her,
so with חליצה, yes, it can be ended,
but with a גט, no.
So the משנה teaches us that a גט works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by showing what mistake the teaching prevents.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without this teaching, we might read 'ויבמה' as keeping the יבום bond alive, so that only חליצה could end it. The משנה teaches that a גט is enough.

steps.title: Isn't remarrying her obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the second half of רבי יוסי בר חנינא's answer: why do we need to be told that he may take her back after divorcing her?
steps.simpleTranslation: He may take her back. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second teaching and asks the same question: why say it? This sets up the next explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any man may normally remarry the wife he divorced. So it seems obvious that this יבם may as well.

keyTerms.meaning: he takes her back (remarries her)

phrases.english: He takes her back. Isn't that obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 15, now asking about the second teaching from step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why it is necessary to say that he may remarry her after the divorce.

steps.title: We might have thought אשת אח comes back
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that once he did the מצוה of יבום, the איסור of אשת אח would come back after the divorce. The משנה teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought this: the Torah put a מצוה on him, and he did it. Now that it is done, she should go back to being forbidden to him as his brother's wife. The משנה teaches us that she does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the mistake here. We might have thought that after the divorce she becomes forbidden to him again as his brother's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אשת אח was only set aside so he could do the מצוה of יבום. Once the מצוה is finished and he divorces her, one might think the original איסור returns. The משנה says he may remarry her, which shows it does not return.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה the Torah placed on him
the איסור of a brother's wife
she should stand / be set back (in her old status)

phrases.english: It could enter your mind to say,
the מצוה that the Merciful One placed on him,
he has done it;
now let her go back to being, for him,
under the איסור of a brother's wife.
So the משנה teaches us that she does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא, מִצְוָה דְּרַמְיָא רַחֲמָנָא עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 with the mistaken idea the teaching prevents.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without this teaching, we might think that once the מצוה is done, the איסור of אשת אח returns after the divorce.

steps.title: Why not say she really is forbidden again?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the reasoning that אשת אח returns sounds logical, so why not accept it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us say it really is so: she is forbidden to him again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling. It asks why the 'mistaken' idea from the last step should not actually be the law. This sets up the source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that אשת אח comes back once the מצוה is done seemed reasonable. So the גמרא needs a source to show why the law is otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: but say it is indeed so

phrases.english: But say it is indeed so, that she is forbidden to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 18 by taking the 'mistaken' idea seriously.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that he may remarry her after divorcing her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The איסור of אשת אח was only set aside for the מצוה. Once the מצוה is done, it should logically come back.

steps.title: Once he takes her, she is fully his wife
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ולקחה לו לאשה' teaches that once he marries her, she is his wife in every way, so אשת אח does not come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And take her to him as a wife.' Once he has taken her, she is like his wife in every way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק. After יבום she is simply his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לו לאשה' make her his own wife, not just a woman tied to him through his brother. A wife he divorced may be remarried, so this one may be too. The same reasoning also explains why a גט ends the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק says
and take her to him as a wife
like his wife in every way

steps.whatToRemember: After יבום, she is his full wife: a גט ends the marriage, and he may remarry her afterward without any איסור of אשת אח.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And take her to him as a wife"
once he has taken her,
she is like his wife in every way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The איסור of אשת אח returns once the מצוה of יבום is done.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ולקחה לו לאשה' makes her his wife in every way, so the איסור does not return and he may remarry her.

steps.title: Why is the כתובה different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's one exception, that her כתובה is still tied to the first husband, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Except that her כתובה is...' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה. That line gives one way she is not like his ordinary wife: her כתובה. The גמרא asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that she is his wife in every way. So it is surprising that her כתובה still comes from the first husband's property. The גמרא wants to know what makes the כתובה an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: except that / provided that
the marriage contract and the money it promises the wife
what is the reason?

phrases.english: "Except that her כתובה shall be..." and so on.
phrases.notes: The משנה's full line says her כתובה is paid from her first husband's property. 'כו׳' just means 'and so on.'

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה, an exception to 'she is his wife in every way.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why her כתובה remains on the first husband's property rather than the יבם's.

steps.title: She was given to him by Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The יבם did not choose this wife himself. Heaven gave her to him, so he never took on her כתובה himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: A wife was given to him by Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כתובה is different because this marriage came to him from Heaven, not by his own choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary husband chooses his wife and takes on her כתובה himself. The יבם got this wife through the Torah's command, so he never made that commitment. Her כתובה therefore stays tied to the first husband's property. This is an exception about the כתובה only; it does not change the fact that she is his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: they gave her to him as his own
from Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: After יבום she is his wife in every way, except that her כתובה stays on the first husband's property, because Heaven gave her to the יבם rather than his choosing her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a difference between being a wife and having a כתובה obligation. The marriage is complete, but the money commitment follows who actually took it on.

phrases.english: A wife was given to him by Heaven.
phrases.notes: He means that the יבם never chose her himself, so he never took on her כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Heaven gave her to the יבם as a wife. He did not take her on by his own choice, so her כתובה remains on the first husband's property.

steps.title: If the first husband left nothing, the כתובה comes from the יבם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a qualification. If the woman cannot collect her כתובה from the first husband's property, the חכמים made the יבם responsible for it, so he won't divorce her too easily.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she has nothing to collect from the first husband, the חכמים set up that she collects from the second, so that she will not seem cheap in his eyes and easy to divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits what it just said. Normally the כתובה is tied to the first husband, but if he left no property, the חכמים made the יבם pay it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 explained that the יבם never took on the כתובה himself, because Heaven gave him this wife. That creates a problem: if the first husband left nothing, the יבם could divorce her for free. So the חכמים made a תקנה that the יבם is responsible, which makes divorce costly and protects her.

keyTerms.meaning: They instituted, meaning the חכמים made a rabbinic enactment (תקנה)
The first husband, the brother who died
The second husband, the יבם
Literally 'light in his eyes', meaning easy for him to send away
To send her out, meaning to divorce her

steps.whatToRemember: The כתובה of a יבמה normally comes from the first husband's property. If there is none, the חכמים made the יבם responsible so he will not divorce her lightly.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common pattern: when the basic דין leaves a woman unprotected, the חכמים step in with a תקנה so that divorce is not cheap.

phrases.english: And if she does not have [what to collect] from the first [husband]
they instituted for her [to collect] from the second

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא קַלָּה בְּעֵינָיו לְהוֹצִיאָהּ
phrases.english: so that she should not be light in his eyes to divorce her

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies Step 22: the rule that the כתובה stays with the first husband has a rabbinic fallback when the first husband left nothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first husband left no property, the חכמים made the יבם responsible for her כתובה so he will not divorce her easily.

steps.title: The eldest brother has the first מצוה of יבום
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: the מצוה of יבום goes first to the eldest brother. If he refuses, the other brothers are asked. If they all refuse, the eldest is told he must do either חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The מצוה is for the eldest to do יבום. If he does not want to, they go around to all the brothers. If they do not want to, they go back to the eldest and tell him: the מצוה is on you, either do חליצה or do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out the order of which brother is asked to do יבום, with the eldest first and last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eldest brother has priority for the מצוה. But his priority also means responsibility: if everyone refuses, the obligation comes back to him and he must choose חליצה or יבום, so the woman is not left stuck.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (here shortened to מַתְנִי׳)
The eldest brother
To do יבום, marrying the dead brother's widow
They go around, meaning בית דין approaches each brother
Do חליצה, the ceremony that releases her from יבום

phrases.english: MISHNA: The מצוה is on the eldest to do yibum

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָצָה — מְהַלְּכִין עַל כׇּל הָאַחִין
phrases.english: If he did not want to, they go around to all the brothers
phrases.notes: 'They' is בית דין, asking each brother in turn.

phrases.english: If they did not want to, they go back to the eldest
and they say to him: The מצוה is on you:
either do chalitza or do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on the order of priority among the brothers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eldest brother has first claim on the מצוה of יבום. If all brothers refuse, he must do either חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: A brother cannot stall by waiting for another brother
steps.stepSummary: If a brother says he will wait for another brother who is a minor, or for the eldest brother who is overseas, or for a brother who is a חרש or שוטה, בית דין does not listen. He must do חליצה or יבום now.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made it depend on a minor until he grows up, or on the eldest until he comes back from overseas, or on a חרש or a שוטה, they do not listen to him. Instead they tell him: the מצוה is on you, either do חליצה or do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. A brother tries to delay by saying 'let's wait for another brother', and the משנה says this excuse is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these brothers cannot act right now: a minor is too young, the one overseas is absent, and a חרש or שוטה cannot do the מצוה at the moment. The brother who is here must act now. The גמרא later explains why: we never delay a מצוה (step 34).

keyTerms.meaning: He made it depend, meaning he put off his decision to wait for someone else
Here: a minor, a brother who is not yet בר מצוה
Overseas, far away
A deaf-mute, who in הלכה is not fully obligated in מצוות
A person without sound mind

steps.confusionAlert: Here קטן means a minor ('until he grows up'). In the very next step, the גמרא uses קטן to mean a younger brother who is an adult. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: If he made it depend on a minor until he grows up
phrases.notes: He's saying: 'Wait for my little brother to grow up. Maybe he'll do יבום, and if not, I will.'

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בַּגָּדוֹל עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם
phrases.english: or on the eldest until he comes from overseas
or on a deaf-mute or an imbecile

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ, אֶלָּא אוֹמְרִים לוֹ:
phrases.english: they do not listen to him; rather, they say to him:

phrases.aramaic: עָלֶיךָ מִצְוָה, אוֹ חֲלוֹץ אוֹ יַיבֵּם.
phrases.english: The מצוה is on you, either do chalitza or do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה: a brother cannot avoid the obligation by waiting for a brother who cannot act now.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית דין does not allow a brother to delay by waiting for a minor, an absent brother, a חרש, or a שוטה. He must do חליצה or יבום now.
steps.whatToRemember: No brother may put off the מצוה by waiting for another brother who cannot act now, not even for the eldest. As the גמרא explains in step 34, we never delay a מצוה.

steps.title: Which is better: a younger brother's יבום or the eldest's חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports a מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי. If a younger brother wants to do יבום and the eldest wants to do חליצה, one says the younger brother's יבום is better, and the other says the eldest's חליצה is better.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was stated: on a younger brother's יבום versus the eldest's חליצה, רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree. One said: the younger brother's יבום is preferable. And one said: the eldest's חליצה is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a new מחלוקת between two אמוראים. The question is which matters more, the act of יבום or the eldest brother's priority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the מצוה goes first to the eldest. But what if the eldest only wants to do חליצה, while a younger brother wants to do the full יבום? One side values doing יבום itself more. The other side values the eldest brother's priority more, even if he only does חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated, which introduces a מחלוקת among אמוראים
יבום done by the younger brother
חליצה done by the eldest brother
They disagree
Is preferable, better

steps.confusionAlert: Here קטן does not mean a minor. It means a younger brother, an adult who is younger than the eldest.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question the rest of the sugya will work on: which is more important, the מצוה of יבום itself or the eldest brother's priority?

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
[regarding] the consummation of the younger and the chalitza of the eldest

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disagree about it
One said: the consummation of the younger is preferable
and one said: the chalitza of the eldest is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה's rule of the eldest's priority and asks how it weighs against a younger brother's יבום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: one אמורא prefers יבום by a younger brother, and the other prefers חליצה by the eldest.

steps.title: The reason behind each side of the argument
steps.stepSummary: One side says יבום by a younger brother is better because the main מצוה is יבום. The other side says that when the eldest is there, a younger brother's יבום counts for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the younger brother's יבום is better holds that the real מצוה is יבום. The one who says the eldest's חליצה is better holds that, when the eldest is present, the younger one's יבום is worth nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each אמורא in the last step holds the way he does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one looks at the type of act: יבום is the real מצוה, so it beats חליצה no matter who does it. Side two looks at the person: the eldest has first rights, so while he is around, a younger brother's יבום does not count as the proper מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: יבום done by the younger brother
חליצה done by the eldest brother
is better, is preferred
it is nothing, it does not count

steps.confusionAlert: In this line, קָטָן means the YOUNGER brother, not a child. By contrast, the משנה (step 25), which the גמרא quotes again later (step 32), uses קָטָן to mean an actual minor.

phrases.english: The one who said: yibum by the younger brother is better —
that is because the מצוה is in yibum itself.
And the one who said: chalitzah by the eldest is better:
where the eldest is present —
yibum by the younger one is nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the two opinions recorded in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: View 1: יבום is the main מצוה, so it wins. View 2: the eldest's priority makes a younger brother's יבום worthless while the eldest is present.

steps.title: A proof from the משנה that the younger brother's יבום is better
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the eldest 'does not want,' we go to the other brothers. The גמרא reads this as: he refuses יבום but is willing to do חליצה, and we still go to the brothers for יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if he does not want, we go around to all the brothers. Doesn't this mean he refused יבום but would do חליצה? And still we go to the brothers. So a younger brother's יבום must be better!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove the first view (younger brother's יבום is better) from the משנה in step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'he does not want' means he only refuses יבום and is willing to do חליצה, then the משנה skips his willing חליצה in favor of a younger brother's יבום. That would show that a younger brother's יבום beats the eldest's חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: we learned in a משנה
we go around to all the brothers
isn't it that…? (opens a suggested reading)
learn from this

phrases.english: We learned: If he did not want —
we go around to all the brothers.
Isn't it that he did not want to do yibum
but only to do chalitzah,
and it teaches: we go to the brothers,
learn from this: yibum by the younger one is better!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: לֹא רָצָה מַחְזִירִין עַל כׇּל הָאַחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the מחלוקת against the משנה, siding with the first view.
steps.raayaObject: The view that a younger brother's יבום is better than the eldest's חליצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'לֹא רָצָה — מַחְזִירִין עַל כׇּל הָאַחִין', read as refusing יבום only

steps.title: The proof is pushed off: he refused both
steps.stepSummary: No. The משנה may mean the eldest refused both חליצה and יבום, so it proves nothing about which act is better.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means he did not want to do חליצה and did not want to do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading 'he does not want' as a full refusal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the eldest refuses everything, going to the other brothers is just the natural next step. It does not show that a younger brother's יבום beats the eldest's חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: to do חליצה
to do יבום

phrases.english: No, he did not want to do chalitzah
and not to do yibum.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לֹא רָצָה לַחְלוֹץ וְלֹא לְיַיבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 28.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed he refused only יבום. The משנה can be read as refusing both acts.

steps.title: Then why go back to the eldest to force him?
steps.stepSummary: If the eldest refused both, then the brothers' refusal must also mean they refused both. So why go back and force the eldest? Just force the brothers!
steps.simpleTranslation: Then in the matching case of the brothers, they also refused both חליצה and יבום. If so, why go back to the eldest to force him? Let בית דין force the brothers!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new reading, everyone has refused everything. So there is no clear reason to return to the eldest instead of forcing one of the brothers already standing there. The משנה's choice to go back to the eldest needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: the matching case, the same way
why?
to force him

phrases.english: The matching case with the brothers:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָצוּ לֹא לַחְלוֹץ וְלֹא לְיַיבֵּם.
phrases.english: they did not want to do chalitzah or yibum.
Why go back to the eldest to force him?
Let them force them — the brothers!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording: 'let them force the brothers.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the push-off in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'לֹא רָצָה' means refusing both acts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If everyone refused everything, returning to the eldest seems pointless. The court could simply force one of the brothers.

steps.title: The מצוה is on the eldest, so we force him
steps.stepSummary: Since the מצוה rests first on the eldest, he is the one בית דין forces.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the מצוה lies on him, he is the one we force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps the 'refused both' reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eldest carries the first duty. Even when all the brothers refuse, the pressure goes back to him. So returning to the eldest makes sense, and the proof from step 28 stays rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: lies on, is placed on
we force

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'he does not want' can mean the eldest refused both acts, so it does not prove that a younger brother's יבום is better. We go back to force the eldest because the מצוה is his first.

phrases.english: Since the מצוה lies on him —
it is him that we force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's ruling through the eldest's primary obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once everyone refuses, the court could force any brother.
steps.terutzMaskana: The eldest has the first duty, so he is the one forced.

steps.title: If a younger brother's יבום is better, why not wait for the minor?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the eldest wants to wait for a minor brother to grow up, we do not listen to him. If a younger brother's יבום is better, why not wait? Maybe the minor will grow up and do יבום!
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if he made it depend on a minor until he grows up, we do not listen to him. But if a younger brother's יבום is better, why not listen? Let us wait. Maybe he will grow up and do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another line of the משנה (from step 25). It seems to argue against the view that a younger brother's יבום is better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a younger brother's יבום beats the eldest's חליצה, waiting for the minor to grow up and do יבום should be worth it. The משנה refuses to wait. That suggests a younger brother's יבום is not preferred.

keyTerms.meaning: made it depend on
until he grows up
we do not listen to him
let us wait

phrases.english: We learned: If he made it depend on a minor until he grows up,
we do not listen to him.
And if yibum by the younger one is better,
why don't we listen to him?
Let us wait — maybe he will grow up and do yibum!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: תָּלָה בְּקָטָן עַד שֶׁיַּגְדִּיל אֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new test from the משנה now points the other way.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that בִּיאַת קָטָן עֲדִיפָא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a younger brother's יבום is better, waiting for the minor to grow up and do יבום should be allowed. The משנה's refusal to wait contradicts that view.

steps.title: Your side has the same problem: the brother overseas
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around. The משנה also refuses to wait for the eldest brother who is overseas, even though, by the other view, his חליצה would be better. So the question from step 32 hits both sides equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your own logic: the משנה says that if a brother asks to wait until the eldest returns from overseas, we do not listen to him. Why not? Let us wait. Maybe he will come back and do חליצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 32's question by showing that the opposite view faces the same difficulty. It does not answer it head-on yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 said: if a younger brother's יבום is better, we should wait for the minor. Here the גמרא replies: if the eldest's חליצה is better, we should wait for him to come back from overseas, yet the משנה says we don't. Since the משנה refuses to wait in both cases, its refusal cannot be the reason to prefer one view.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning a question back on the one who asked it
Overseas, a faraway land
We do not listen to him; his request is not accepted
Let us wait
Performs חליצה

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the גמרא's final answer. It only shows that the question from step 32 works just as well against the other side. The real answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: But according to your reasoning,
phrases.notes: He means: by the view that the eldest brother's חליצה is better than a younger brother's יבום.

phrases.english: and with the eldest, waiting until he comes from overseas,
we do not listen to him. Why not?
Let us wait; perhaps he will come and do חליצה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 32 by showing that the other side faces the same difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the eldest brother's חליצה is better
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the eldest's חליצה is better, the משנה should wait for him to return from overseas, but it does not.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the same difficulty applies to both views (ולטעמיך)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Refusing to wait for the minor proves a younger brother's יבום is not better.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה also refuses to wait for the eldest, so refusing to wait proves nothing either way.

steps.title: The real reason: we never delay a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the true reason for both rulings: we do not hold back a מצוה. So the משנה's refusal to wait says nothing about which brother or which act is better.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we do not delay any מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real explanation that covers both cases: we never delay a מצוה that can be done now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether the brother who is missing is a minor or is overseas, a brother who is here now can do the מצוה, and we do not put it off. That is the only reason the משנה refuses to wait. So the attempted proof from the משנה about which act or brother is preferred falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: brings in the real explanation
Delaying a מצוה
We do not delay

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה refuses to wait for the minor or for the brother overseas only because we never delay a מצוה. So it proves nothing about which act or which brother is better.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a general rule: a מצוה that can be done now should not be put off in the hope of doing it in a better way later.

phrases.english: Rather, any delaying of a מצוה
we do not delay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real reason behind both cases raised in steps 32 and 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule that explains both rulings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The refusal to wait shows which act or which brother is preferred.
steps.terutzMaskana: The refusal to wait comes only from the rule that we do not delay a מצוה, so no proof can be drawn.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We do not delay a מצוה; the משנה's refusal to wait proves nothing about which act or brother is better.
